summary: Comments is a thread pinned to one spot in a design, where people reply to each other and can bring the agent in by typing @agent. Each comment is an avatar, a name, a time and the text; the first one starts the thread and the replies sit indented under it on a thin line. A quiet Agree button shows beside the time on hover or keyboard focus. The agent's reply shows a thinking mark first, then its words fade in, and it can end with buttons such as Apply to all that turn into a short note once used. The whole thread can be resolved, which fades it back.
use: When feedback lives on a design or document and the agent should act on it from the thread
When people need to @mention teammates and the agent from the same reply field
When an agent's suggestion needs a yes or a choice before it changes anything
When resolved threads should stay visible but step back
features: The first of `comments` starts the thread, and every later one is a reply, indented under it on a thin line. The header counts the replies.
Typing @ and the start of a handle opens a menu of matching `people`, and Enter or a click inserts the handle.
@mentions in plain text comments are highlighted in the accent's tint, limited to known handles when `people` is given.

Each comment's Agree button shows on hover or keyboard focus, and always on a touch screen. It toggles yours in `agreed`, and a chip under the text counts everyone who agreed (`agrees` on the comment, plus you); the chip toggles yours too.
A comment with `thinking` shows the thinking dots; an `agent` comment's words fade in as its `text` grows.
`actions` add buttons under a comment, and setting `resolution` replaces them with a confirmation line like "Applied to 3 frames".
Enter or the Send button calls `onSend` with the trimmed reply and clears the field; Send is disabled while the field is empty.
The reply field has a dimmed edge at rest and a step stronger one while it has the focus, with no ring.
The Resolve button in the header toggles `resolved`, fades the thread, turns the pin green and marks the thread Resolved.
a11y: The thread is an `aria-live="polite"` region, so new comments and replies are announced, and the replies are a group labelled Replies.
The reply field is a `combobox` with `aria-expanded` reflecting the mention menu, which is a `listbox` of `option` rows.
In the mention menu ↑ and ↓ move the highlight and wrap, which `aria-activedescendant` points to, and Enter picks the highlighted person.
Escape dismisses the mention menu until the text changes.
Agree and its chip are toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`; the chip's label says how many agreed. The Agree button stays in the tab order and shows as soon as it has the focus.
Resolve thread reports its state with `aria-pressed`, and the icon-only Send button has an `aria-label`.

faq.q: How do I stream the agent's reply into the thread?
faq.a: Add a comment with `agent: true` and `thinking: true`, then set `thinking` to false and keep updating its `text` as tokens arrive. Each word fades in as it is added.

faq.q: Does the component call my agent when someone types @agent?
faq.a: No. `onSend` gives you the reply text, and you decide what happens. The example checks for @agent, adds the person's comment, then adds the agent's reply.

faq.q: How do I let the person approve the agent's change?
faq.a: Give the agent's comment `actions`, such as Apply to all and Just this one. In each `onClick`, apply the change and set `resolution` to a short line that replaces the buttons.

faq.q: How do I save who agreed with a comment?
faq.a: Pass `agreed` with the ids of the comments the current person agreed with, and update it in `onAgreedChange`. Put everyone else's count in each comment's `agrees`.
